ado

Update installed packages

Stata 

ado update

R utils 

update.packages()

Stata reference · R reference

capture

Run code and keep its result without stopping on an error

Stata 

capture command

R tidystata 

capture(expression)

Differs from Stata Returns the expression's result on success; on error, emits a failure message and returns invisible NULL. quiet = TRUE suppresses the notice, warnings and messages, but keeps printed output. Use capture(data <- update(data)) to preserve an existing object if the update fails; data <- capture(update(data)) assigns NULL on error. Separate assignments in a captured block keep the last completed update; a single assignment around a failed pipeline keeps the original target. Earlier effects are not rolled back. This adapts Stata capture, which suppresses all output.

display

A stored coefficient

Stata 

display _b[x]

R stats 

coef(fit)["x"]

Stata reference · R reference

A stored standard error

Stata 

display _se[x]

R stats 

sqrt(diag(vcov(fit)))["x"]

Stata reference · R reference

foreach

Same calculation for several variables

Stata 

foreach v of varlist v1-v5 { generate `v'_sq = `v'^2 }

R dplyr 

mutate(data, across(v1:v5, ~ .x^2, .names = "{col}_sq"))

across() replaces most variable loops; for other loops R has for (v in names) { ... }.

Stata reference · R reference

forvalues

Loop with a condition

Stata 

forvalues i = 1/5 { generate v`i'_sq = v`i'^2 if v`i' > 0 }

R dplyr 

mutate(data, across(v1:v5, ~ if_else(.x > 0, .x^2, NA), .names = "{col}_sq"))

Stata reference · R reference

Loop over variables numbered in their names

Stata 

forvalues i = 6/10 { forvalues j = 3/5 { replace x_`i'_`j' = x_`i'_`j' + 1 } }

R dplyr 

mutate(data, across(matches("^x_([6-9]|10)_[3-5]$"), ~ .x + 1))

A regular expression picks the names. varlist("x_[6-10]_*") works when only one number range is needed.

Stata reference · R reference

frame

Hold another dataset

Stata 

frame create other

R tibble 

other <- tibble()

R keeps any number of data frames as separate objects, so frames are built in.

Stata reference · R reference

if

Run code only if a condition holds

Stata 

if `x' > 0 { display "positive" }

R base 

if (x > 0) print("positive")

Quote it: findit("if"), because if is a reserved word in R.

Stata reference · R reference

local

Store a list of variable names

Stata 

local vars x1 x2 x3

R base 

vars <- c("x1", "x2", "x3")

Use it with all_of(): select(data, all_of(vars)) or across(all_of(vars), ...).

Stata reference · R reference

matrix

Create a matrix

Stata 

matrix A = (1, 2 \ 3, 4)

R base 

A <- matrix(c(1, 2, 3, 4), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)

Stata reference · R reference

preserve

Keep a copy to return to

Stata 

preserve

R base 

backup <- data

Differs from Stata Keeps a backup of an ordinary data frame; restore with data <- backup. Reference objects such as data.table require their own copy rules.

Stata reference · R reference

program

Write your own command

Stata 

program define myprog

R base 

myprog <- function(data) { summ(data) }

Stata reference · R reference

quietly

Run without printing

Stata 

quietly regress y x

R stats 

fit <- lm(y ~ x, data = data)

Assigning a result never prints it; print(fit) or summary(fit) shows it later.

Stata reference · R reference

scalar

Store a single number

Stata 

scalar a = 3

R base 

a <- 3

Stata reference · R reference

set

Make random numbers reproducible

Stata 

set seed 2024

R base 

set.seed(2024)

Differs from Stata set_seed(.fn, seed) sets the seed inside a pipe; see the sample rows. R and Stata use different random-number streams; the same numeric seed does not reproduce the same draws or selected rows.

Stata reference · R reference

tempfile

A temporary file

Stata 

tempfile f

R base 

f <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")

Temporary variables are not needed: intermediate columns can be dropped, or kept as separate objects.
